card: Adds a preparation job in GitHub Actions to check out qa-assets once per workflow run and distribute unit test vectors and fuzz corpora as compressed workflow artifacts. Currently, each CI job across multiple platforms downloads identical test assets independently, causing intermittent HTTP 504 timeouts and CI run failures before tests start (#36814). Downstream jobs verify revision and SHA-256 file hashes before running tests, mounting inputs read-only in containers or creating isolated working copies for fuzzing.
changed_since_previous: Diff provided for the initial implementation, confirming tar-based artifact packaging, SHA-256 manifest verification, and unified CLI handling in test/download_utils.py.
evidence: PR description: 'As reported in #36814, these repeated requests can fail with HTTP 504 before the tests start.'
Referenced issue #36814: 'ci: Repeated downloads of shared test assets cause intermittent job failures'
problem: Multiple CI jobs across Linux, macOS, and Windows independently clone or download the same qa-assets repository, wasting network bandwidth and causing intermittent CI job failures due to HTTP 504 gateway timeouts.

risk.why: Mistakes in the CI asset pipeline would cause test jobs to fail to start or report corrupted assets in CI, with no impact on node runtime or consensus.

scope_notes: Touches CI workflow files across GitHub Actions, container setup scripts, Windows CI runner scripts, and utility download scripts in test/download_utils.py.
summary: Introduces a dedicated GitHub Actions job to checkout bitcoin-core/qa-assets once per workflow run and share unit test vectors and fuzz corpora as workflow artifacts. Adds a manifest verification mechanism in test/download_utils.py to ensure downloaded assets match expected git revisions and file SHA-256 hashes. Downstream test jobs restore the tarred artifacts, mount them read-only in containers, or make separate writable copies for fuzz targets.
